'''Gennadi Sardanashvily''' ({{langx|ru|Генна́дий Алекса́ндрович Сарданашви́ли}}; March 13, 1950 – September 1, 2016) was a [[theoretical physicist]], a principal research scientist of [[Moscow State University]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Obituary of Professor Gennadi Sardanashvily |author-last=Krupka |author-first=Demeter |author-link=:cs:Demeter Krupka |date=2016-10-16 |url=https://www.lepageri.eu/files/Obituary-Gennadi-Sardanashvily.pdf |access-date=2026-09-27 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170603223653/https://www.lepageri.eu/files/Obituary-Gennadi-Sardanashvily.pdf |archive-date=2017-06-03 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |title=Obituary of Professor Gennadi Sardanashvily |url=http://www.worldscientific.com/page/ijgmmp/Gennadi-Sardanashvily |journal=International Journal of Geometric Methods in Modern Physics }}{{Dead link|date=August 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Rossi |first1=Olga |author-link1=:d:Q95463743 |title=Editorial |journal=Communications in Mathematics |date=1 December 2016 |volume=24 |issue=2 |pages=89–89 |issn=1804-1388 |doi=10.1515/cm-2016-fm |doi-access=free}}</ref>

== Biography ==
Gennadi Sardanashvily graduated from [[Moscow State University]] (MSU) in 1973, he was a Ph.D. student of  the Department of Theoretical Physics ([[Moscow State University|MSU]]) in 1973&ndash;76, where he held a position in 1976.

He attained his Ph.D. degree in physics and mathematics from [[Moscow State University|MSU]], in 1980, with [[Dmitri Ivanenko]] as his supervisor, and his D.Sc. degree in physics and mathematics from [[Moscow State University|MSU]], in 1998.

Gennadi Sardanashvily was the founder and Managing Editor (2003 - 2013) of the [[International Journal of Geometric Methods in Modern Physics]] (IJGMMP).

He was a member of Lepage Research Institute (Slovakia).

==Research area==

Gennadi Sardanashvily research area is geometric method in [[classical mechanics|classical]] and [[quantum mechanics]] and [[classical field theory|field theory]], [[gravitation|gravitation theory]]. His main achievement is geometric formulation of [[classical field theory]] and [[non-autonomous mechanics]] including:

* [[gauge gravitation theory]], where gravity is treated as a [[Higgs field (classical)|classical Higgs field]] associated to a reduced Lorentz structure on a world manifold<ref>[[Dmitri Ivanenko|''D. Ivanenko'']], ''G. Sardanashvily'', The gauge treatment of gravity, Physics Reports '''94''' (1983) 1&ndash;45.</ref>
* geometric formulation of [[classical field theory]]<ref>''G. Giachetta, L. Mangiarotti, G. Sardanashvily'', Lagrangian supersymmetries depending on derivatives. Global analysis and cohomology, Commun. Math. Phys. '''295''' (2005) 103&ndash;128; {{arXiv|hep-th/0407185}}.</ref> and Lagrangian [[BRST formalism|BRST]] theory<ref>''D. Bashkirov, G. Giachetta, L. Mangiarotti, G. Sardanashvily'', The KT-BRST complex of a degenerate Lagrangian theory, Lett. Math. Phys. '''83''' (2008) 237&ndash;252; {{arXiv|math-ph/0702097}}.</ref> where classical fields are represented by sections of [[fiber bundle]]s and their dynamics is described in terms of [[jet bundle|jet manifolds]] and the [[variational bicomplex]] ([[covariant classical field theory]])
* [[covariant Hamiltonian field theory|covariant (polysymplectic) Hamiltonian field theory]], where momenta correspond to derivatives of fields with respect to all world coordinates<ref>''G. Giachetta, L. Mangiarotti, G. Sardanashvily'', Covariant Hamiltonian equations for field theory, J. Phys. A '''32''' (1999) 6629&ndash;6642; {{arXiv|hep-th/9904062}}.</ref>
* the [[Noether's second theorem|second Noether theorem]] in a very general setting of [[Noether identities|reducible degenerate]] Grassmann-graded [[Lagrangian system]]s on an arbitrary manifold<ref>''G. Giachetta, L. Mangiarotti, G. Sardanashvily'', On the notion of gauge symmetries of generic Lagrangian field theory, J. Math. Phys. '''50''' (2009) 012903; {{arXiv|0807.3003}}.</ref>
* geometric formulation of classical<ref>''G. Sardanashvily'', Hamiltonian time-dependent mechanics, J. Math. Phys. '''39''' (1998) 2714&ndash;2729.</ref> and quantum<ref>''L.Mangiarotti, G. Sardanashvily'', Quantum mechanics with respect to different reference frames, J. Math. Phys. '''48''' (2007) 082104; {{arXiv|quant-ph/0703266}}.</ref>  [[non-autonomous mechanics]] on [[fiber bundle]]s over <math>\mathbb R</math>
* generalization of the Liouville&ndash;Arnold, Nekhoroshev and Mishchenko&ndash;Fomenko theorems on  [[integrable system|completely]] and [[integrable system|partially integrable]] and [[superintegrable Hamiltonian system]]s to the case of non-compact invariant submanifolds<ref>''E. Fiorani, G. Sardanashvily'', Global action-angle coordinates for completely integrable systems with non-compact invariant submanifolds, J. Math. Phys. '''48''' (2007) 032901; {{arXiv|math/0610790}}.</ref>
* cohomology of the [[variational bicomplex]] of [[graded manifold|graded differential forms]] of finite jet order on an infinite order jet manifold.<ref>''G. Sardanashvily'', Graded infinite order jet manifolds, Int. J. Geom. Methods Mod. Phys. '''4''' (2007) 1335&ndash;1362; {{arXiv|0708.2434}}</ref>

Gennadi Sardanashvily has published more than 400 scientific works, including 28 books.
